newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr/mark at 8-year high, Euro stocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr/mark at 8-year high, Euro stocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar's rampaging bull run was intact on Tuesday morning with the U.S. currency testing its eight-year high against the mark.

Most European stock markets also advanced amid solid corporate earnings, relief Wall Street managed to erase steep opening losses on Monday to close higher and expectations the strong dollar will boost European exports.

Despite a brief setback in late European trading on Monday when some investors sold dollars to lock in profits made in the unit's recent rally, the dollar retained its bullish tone and resumed its climb versus the mark.
Investors started buying dollars again on relief Germany's central bank stuck to its planned, fixed 3.0-percent weekly money market operation.

Some traders had speculated the Bundesbank would surprise the market and also announce a variable-rate operation to allow rates to drift up and lift the mark from near eight-year lows versus the dollar.

"Dollar/mark will soon be testing new highs, given the Bundesbank has done nothing today and that it will be another week before we find out what they are going to do about rates," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International.

Analysts said the market was now aiming to push the dollar up to 1.90 marks from about 1.8695 in early trade, especially if German jobs data on Wednesday show little improvement in cutting joblessness.
A clearer path for the dollar to rise against the mark calmed Germany's stock market, which shed about two percent on Monday because of German interest rate jitters.
Mark weakness makes German goods cheaper abroad, which should boost exports.
Further comfort came from Wall Street's recovery late in the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 4.41 points at 8,198.45 after being down more than 50 points shortly after the open.
The Dow got a lift from technology stocks, which soared to pull the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index up 11 points to a record 1,605.

But Paris traders were not yet convinced German rate threats were gone. The blue-chip CAC-40 index slipped into negative ground by midday after the German Ifo economic research institute said the Bundesbank might send a signal to currency markets if the dollar rose above 1.90 marks.
"I could imagine that a dollar above 1.90 marks would set alarm bells ringing in Frankfurt," said Ifo economist Willi Leibfritz.
A trader in Paris said "there are real worries about tension on rates. People are watching the Bundesbank closely."
London shares also had rate worries looming. The Bank of England (BOE) meets on Wednesday and Thursday to determine monetary policy.
"I'm afraid that the uncertainty about interest rates will keep volumes low and markets volatile," a dealer said.
But until then, London traders said corporate earnings would drive market moves. The FTSE jumped more than a percent by midday, led by the oil and drug sectors.

British Petroleum Co Plc hit a year high of 850 pence after the firm said second-quarter replacement cost net profit before exceptionals was 740 million pounds, up from 648 million a year ago and analysts' forecasts between 630 and 690 million pounds.
British Petroleum also said it planned to buy back shares from "time to time."

BAA Plc jumped after the airport management group said pre-tax profits for the three months ending June 30 rose to 136 million pounds ($222 million), in line with analysts' forecasts between 134 million and 140 million sterling.
Just before midday, BAA shares were up 18 pence at 579, just off its session high of 582.
National Westminster Bank shares tumbled after earnings failed to meet analysts' expectations.

The bank said first half pre-tax profits rose to 669 million pounds versus 302 million last year and pre-tax profits from continuing operations rose to 775 million from 662 million. That compares with analysts' forecasts for pre-tax profits between 757 million and 770 million sterling.
Natwest shares were down 32 pence at 839, off its session low of 834-3/4.

Swedish forestry company Stora AB said a stronger market drove delivery volumes up 10 percent in the first half but lower prices capped its profits, which fell 24 percent. It said profits after financial items was 1.22 billion crowns, better than analysts' expectatioms for a 30-percent drop to 1.13 billion crowns ($140.4 million).
Stora shares were up 2.0 crowns at 133.50, just off its session high of 134.
In metals, palladium was fixed at $245.50, a 17-year high.
